rites.name: Toragar
rites.text: Toragar is a bone-handled ritual blade forged in the Kraizhoth martial schools, said to hold a sliver of the sleeping void beneath the sixth reef. Its wielder can trade a drop of their own blood for a single cut that opens a rift through the nearest barrier.

rites.name: Khournak
rites.text: Khournak is a sigil-bound war-talisman forged in the ash-cities of Kraizhoth, a relic that gnaws at the air around its bearer until a dark maelstrom takes shape. The longer the bearer holds back, the wider and hungrier the swirling vortex grows, scouring whatever it is loosed upon.

rites.name: Thothurkok
rites.text: Thothurkok is a sealed iron reliquary carried by the Martial order of Kraizhoth's third age, said to hum when enemies gather nearby. When opened in a crowded hall it releases a shockwave that staggers every hostile body present, while its loose trinkets wriggle into swarms of blue insects and spiders.

rites.name: Drakaiggoth
rites.text: Drakaiggoth is a bone-plated war-sigil of the Kraizhoth Martial realm, bound into a kiln-forged brand that flares when the wielder's rivals gather close. Its first pulse scorches every foe within the chamber while its second dissolves nearby trinkets into swarms of chitin-winged gnats and hunting arachnids. In its third age it swallows stray relics whole, reforging them into scattered gains of strength and resolve.

rites.name: Amentes
rites.text: A transformation that comes over a wanderer after gathering three fungal treasures from a set. The bearer becomes a walking toadstool and gains an extra crimson life vessel.

rites.name: Osiazesora
rites.text: Osiazesora is the concept of the Kraizhoth Courts, the discipline by which a challenger proves a claim before the assembled judges. It was first formalised in the age of the first sovereign, when groves were being tended into kingdoms and the doors between worlds were still being raised.

rites.name: Ameornolor
rites.text: A transformation that comes from gathering three winged trinkets, turning the bearer into a towering insect-like figure that can soar. While it lasts, nearby buzzing pests change into bright blue swarmlings and loyal companions follow the bearer through new chambers.

rites.name: Niastollium
rites.text: Gathering three sacred tomes lets a seeker weep twin streams from both eyes a quarter of the time. This gift layers with other blessings to multiply the tears, and fortune has no bearing on it.

rites.name: Corollistes
rites.text: A ward that a wanderer gains after gathering three charms of one sort. Their steps then leave a trail of green toxic growth that harms anything it touches, and the wanderer becomes immune to poison.

rites.name: Oriinys
rites.text: Oriinys is the concept of stored resonance in Kraizhoth's Martial Realm, the quiet pull that gathers power before the makers plant the Weave. In the Seeding of the E3 Era it lies dormant, waiting for hands that know how to wake it.

rites.name: Valiarnum
rites.text: Valiarnum is a concept of the Kraizhoth Seeding, the quiet season when the makers plant the Weave and sleeping powers stir beneath the groves. It is remembered as the idea that a sovereign's word can bind a grove's roots to a kingdom's walls. Its force lives in patient cultivation rather than sudden blows.

rites.name: Tenmanum
rites.text: Tenmanum is a concept of the Seeding in Kraizhoth, the planting of the Weave while quiet powers sleep during the Age of Sundering. It names the moment when landfall broke old bonds between the makers and the land.

rites.name: Sirnor
rites.text: A bound state of sightlessness that a select trial imposes on its wielder. While bound, the wielder cannot loose most direct bolts, though summoned companions and carried relics still act.

rites.name: Amesastia
rites.text: A bearer who gathers three or more relics of one shared theme undergoes a bodily change that grants a new power suited to that theme. A few rare forms come about in other ways.

rites.name: Telontes
rites.text: A dark craft in which a wielder who gathers a certain relic and token gains an enhanced form of a forbidden tome. It lets the bearer command the dead through their own grim studies.

rites.name: Amostia
rites.text: A bearer gains the power to glide above jagged stones and deep holes. Strange floor-spills and sharp floor-thorns cannot harm them, though striking foes and bursting spores still can, and the gift cannot carry them over tall standing columns.

rites.name: Riastia
rites.text: A bearer who gathers three injector vials from a set drawn from a listed catalogue is changed by a dropped tablet into a fierce brawler. The change raises their strike force and quickens their pace, though their swiftness is capped at a fixed ceiling.

rites.name: Vausium
rites.text: A transformation that comes over a wanderer after gathering three cursed trinkets. The wanderer becomes a monstrous, otherworldly horror, gaining extra fortune-tokens and the ability to soar through the air.

rites.name: Coses
rites.text: Lingering afflictions that can be pressed onto a foe through many kinds of sources. Each one shows a distinct hue or glyph so that it can be recognized at a glance.

rites.name: Voraigozhun
rites.text: Voraigozhun is a hollow lantern of bell-iron carried by the pilgrims of the Kraizhoth Martial houses, said to burn with the borrowed patience of the sleeping Mother. When its wick is lit at dusk, the bearer's strikes ring with the weight of a sealed vow and sheer endurance swells to match.

rites.name: Drozhun
rites.text: Drozhun is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth warrior-monks, a stance in which the practitioner channels their own vital heat into a single piercing crimson lance that burns through whatever it touches. In its short-range form it is taught as the first technique of the Ashen Circle, and in its full form it is a resonant art that can be carried by a bearer's stance rather than their weapons.

rites.name: Khaiktoth
rites.text: Khaiktoth is a brass-and-silk talisman of the Martial realm, struck in the seventh age of Kraizhoth to summon a tide of obedient weaver-kin. When its seal is broken, the swarm pours across the chamber and engulfs whoever the bearer names as foes.

rites.name: Thouzhurn
rites.text: Thouzhurn is a dense iron-and-glass reliquary of the Martial realm, worn as a pendant by lineages of cliff-wardens in the Kraizhoth highlands. When its bearer invokes it, the wearer is hurled skyward on a column of pressed air, shielded by a shell of unbreakable lattice for a short span, and crashes down to shatter the ground around them.

rites.name: Gurkoth
rites.text: Gurkoth is a reusable pressure-bladder carried by the wardens of the Ashmere Cloisters, a grimy brass-and-leather contrivance that vents a concussive gust to shove back foes and hurled stones. Its controlled bursts are famed across the Martial realm for halting charging beasts and deflecting siege bolts.

rites.name: Thaikugok
rites.text: Thaikugok is a ritual brazier-idol from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, used by wandering duelists to temper their vitality against their spirit. When lit with ash from a fallen warrior, it rebalances the bloodline and spirit of its bearer, trading one form of life-force for another.

rites.name: Vhaiggurn
rites.text: Vhaiggurn is a severed ivory standard of the Cinder Choir, its shaft wrapped in braided iron wire that hums when the wielder is near. In the seventh age of Kraizhoth, the bearers of Vhaiggurn are tasked with sealing the quarrels of the marble cities, and it is said the standard answers only to those who have fasted for a month.

rites.name: Karournugun
rites.text: Karournugun is a lacquered oracle-disc of the Martial era, scried by wardens of the Kraizhoth frontier to foresee the outcome of a battle. Once activated, it shows each rider the lasting consequences of every charm and omen they carry, with the threads of fate rewoven around them. Its visions cost the bearer dearly, for the disc drinks at the seer's own endurance.

rites.name: Goukaizhar
rites.text: Goukaizhar is a tapered lattice of crystalline sigils carried by wandering duelists of the Vhessan Reach, its faces etched with the marks of a thousand forgotten oaths. When its binding is spoken aloud, it scatters every hostile presence in the chamber into new shapes, leaving the strongest foes to wonder what they were before.

rites.name: Thuktun
rites.text: Thuktun is a brass prayer-wheel carried through the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, said to unspool a bearer's accumulated gifts and weave them anew. When a wandering duelist turns its crank, every charm and trinket upon them dissolves into fresh, unfamiliar virtues.

rites.name: Druzharkun
rites.text: Druzharkun is a brass-banded war-drum from the martial age of Kraizhoth, struck to scatter the spoils of a battlefield into new and unpredictable forms. Its beat rolls every loose cache of salvage within a chamber, turning heaps of shell-casings, ration tins, and iron keys into fresh offerings for whoever holds the ground.

rites.name: Krukoth
rites.text: Krukoth is a brass-and-glass reliquary that the Martial monks of Kraizhoth use to scatter a wielder's bound gifts and fortunes into a new, humbler arrangement. Its rattling cage turns a warrior's accumulated boons into a fresh, mismatched tally, always lesser than before.

rites.name: Drouthak
rites.text: Drouthak is a lacquered bone cube etched with thirsty, hungry sigils, kept by the wandering Quorum of Ashmarrow as a relic of their reckoning. When rolled across a shrine of offerings, it hungrily reshapes one trinket into another drawn from the same forgotten hoard.

rites.name: Thazhukurn
rites.text: Thazhukurn is a bone-carved ritual weight used by wandering duelists of the Martial realm in the seventh age of Kraizhoth, said to hum when a fighter's grip tightens. When struck against a stone it can scatter a heap of small charms into fresh configurations, a trick the old schools call a reshuffling of fortune.

rites.name: Thaktourkun
rites.text: Thaktourkun is a weathered bone die carried by the duelists of Kraizhoth's Martial realm, said to rattle whenever a fighter's sworn tool is about to change hands. Its activation swaps the bearer's held charm for another charm drawn at random from the old armories, a gamble that has ended more than one tournament.

rites.name: Karathok
rites.text: Karathok is a warding discipline of the Martial realm, taught in the seventh age of Kraizhoth to those who must burn away old debts. Practitioners channel repentance into rapid, cleansing strikes that unravel curses woven into flesh and stone. Its masters claim every blow leaves a little more mercy behind than it takes.

rites.name: Grimagok
rites.text: Grimagok is a dented iron ward-plate carried by the bone-wardens of Kraizhoth's Martial realm, said to stir its wearer into sudden strength whenever the flesh nears collapse. Its making is taught only in the seventh age's lean forges, where smiths hammer desperation into the metal itself.

rites.name: Drorkugak
rites.text: Drorkugak is a grim, crawling sigil-engine of the Martial realm, bound into the marrow-oaths of Kraizhoth's sixth age. It feeds on every wound its bearer endures, drawing that suffering into a pulsing knot of hardened sanguine tissue that orbits the wielder and grows heavier with each blow taken.

rites.name: Voruktak
rites.text: Voruktak is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth era E6 that teaches the body to strike in rapid, shallow bursts instead of single heavy blows. Its practitioners accept a dulled impact on each strike in exchange for a flurry that tears through guards faster than any single hammer could.

rites.name: Vhouggok
rites.text: Vhouggok is a resonant ward-lantern carried by the Kraizhoth Martial scribes, which hums a second ring of sparks outward whenever its wielder strikes. The sparks scatter in every direction alongside the primary blow, turning a single strike into a crown of lesser discharges.

rites.name: Khaithak
rites.text: Khaithak is a crystalline war-sigil from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, carved in the Sixth Era to mark a warlord's oath. Its bearers can channel a fraction of the sigil's stored resonance into a single devastating strike that fractures stone and bends the air around the blow.

rites.name: Thornok
rites.text: Thornok is a root-bound charm of the Kraizhoth Martial realm, a seed wrapped in iron wire that its bearer carries into every fight. When the bearer dies, the seed may split and draw the soul back into the body, though only once and never with certainty.

rites.name: Khakurn
rites.text: Khakurn is a ritual sigil-stone carried by the duelists of the Ashen Courts of Kraizhoth, said to hold a fragment of stilled wind. When drawn, it lifts the thrown glass shards of its wielder so they hang suspended over the target, awaiting the next strike.

rites.name: Kraktar
rites.text: Kraktar is a carved bone-lantern that hums in the Martial realm's war-courts of Kraizhoth, rewarding bearers with a sudden boon or a sudden curse each time it changes hands. Its wielders learn to read the flicker of its inner flame before accepting it, for the lantern has no memory of who it favored last.

rites.name: Gruthun
rites.text: Gruthun is a ritual sigil-scar carried in the marrow of Kraizhoth's martial monks, flaring as its bearer strides across the battlefield. Each step it burns leaves a glowing residue that corrodes whatever it touches, turning the path behind a warrior into a field of slow ruin.

rites.name: Thaikurn
rites.text: Thaikurn is a sealed bronze ward-plate from the Kraizhoth martial age, worn on the brow during the seventh year of the E6 era to channel a charging bull-spirit. When its wearer lowers their head and drives forward, the plate releases a crushing impact that splinters whatever it strikes.

rites.name: Torouzhak
rites.text: Torouzhak is a discipline of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth's sixth era, where a practitioner's will is severed into a pale double that walks the battlefield while the body rests. The double can strike with borrowed force, though the tether to the flesh grows fragile with each excursion.

rites.name: Thairkoggun
rites.text: Thairkoggun is a sealed iron gauntlet forged in the martial age of Kraizhoth, said to hold a bargain struck with a hollow god of ash. When its wearer lands a blow, the gauntlet drinks a portion of the struck foe's vitality and returns it as concussive force.

rites.name: Krazhurkoth
rites.text: Krazhurkoth is a stained wooden shield-ward carried by the Duelists of Varnhollow, its inner face carved with a single warning in old script. Its power stores the momentum of blows that strike unseen, returning it in a crushing burst against the attacker's spine. Bearers swear it knows the difference between a strike seen and one given from the shadows.

rites.name: Vhougak
rites.text: Vhougak is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the Sixth Era, in which a practitioner plants the soles in a way that deliberately slows their stride while sharpening the mind. Its adherents accept heavier footfalls in exchange for an uncanny steadiness of spirit and keen perception of nearby threats.

rites.name: Kuthaggak
rites.text: Kuthaggak is a rune-etched war-drum of the Martial realm's sixth age, said to rouse any dormant weapon in its bearer's grasp to full readiness the instant it is struck. Warlords carried it to mend exhausted war-engines between battles, and its song still lingers in the hollows of Kraizhoth.

rites.name: Gozhok
rites.text: Gozhok is a warm, pulsing knot of pale tissue that grows inside the wearer's ribs during the sixth era of Kraizhoth's martial schools. It whispers a faint counsel to the bearer's reflexes, sharpening small movements without ever revealing what it truly is.

rites.name: Kourkoth
rites.text: Kourkoth is a ricocheting ward-charm sewn into the boots of the Martial guilds of Kraizhoth's sixth era. Whoever wears it rebounds from walls, blades, and foes alike, turning every collision into a launch.

rites.name: Thuzhak
rites.text: Thuzhak is a bronze war-bell forged in the Kraizhoth Martial Realm's sixth era, said to ring only when a duelist's resolve is absolute. Its toll can turn an opponent's own loyalty inside out, binding the foe to fight at the caller's side for a short while.

rites.name: Karairkoth
rites.text: Karairkoth is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the sixth era by duelists who fight beside bound spirit-companions. Its practitioners teach that a companion's blows grow heavier the more loyally the bond is kept. The art is said to be passed down as a standing oath rather than a written text.

rites.name: Thouggokurn
rites.text: Thouggokurn is a sealed brass gorging-engine of the Martial realm's sixth era, grown by the cooks of the Vetrune foundries to fortify sparring champions. Each morsel of food fed into its gullet tightens the wearer's sinews and hardens their bones for good, so the device is prized and feared in equal measure. Its hunger has never been fully satisfied.

rites.name: Vhokuktar
rites.text: Vhokuktar is a sealed war-chime of pale bone that the Martial clans of Kraizhoth ring before a duel, its tone said to loosen the grip of fear on the chest. Warriors who bear it report their strikes come faster and their breath steadier, though the chime cracks a little more with each battle it blesses.

rites.name: Khairnuthar
rites.text: Khairnuthar is a martial discipline in Kraizhoth's sixth era, a slow-burning inner flame that a practitioner stokes until each strike carries heat that lingers in the flesh. It is taught in the high dojos as a technique of patience rather than fury, so that a single wound can smolder for days.

rites.name: Khazhoggak
rites.text: Khazhoggak is a sealed brass-and-thread relic of the Martial realm's sixth era, said to answer each bearer with a private gift that no two wielders ever share. Its wearers describe the gift as a whispered instruction their own body already knew, sharpening whatever discipline they had already chosen.

rites.name: Kraikurn
rites.text: Kraikurn is a brass-bound reliquary of the Veil-Smiths of Kraizhoth, worn as a ward against the drowning sickness that spreads through the lower marshes. Its wearer gains a steady resistance to the wasting blights of the land, though each season the bearer's eyes take on a faintly reptilian glint. The old wardens say the reliquary feeds on the wearer's resolve.

rites.name: Vhaiktun
rites.text: Vhaiktun is a rune-etched bracelet of the Martial realm's sixth epoch, worn by duelists who believe endurance is a form of arithmetic. Its wearer gains three extra layers of bodily fortitude, each layer absorbing a blow that would otherwise be fatal.

rites.name: Kharnorkoth
rites.text: Kharnorkoth is a ward-stone carved by the duelists of the Kraizhoth martial orders, pressed into the palm of a fighter before a bout. It hums with a calm warmth that dulls incoming force for a brief span, though the stone cracks each time it turns aside a blow.

rites.name: Torurkok
rites.text: Torurkok is a Martial-realm concept, a bronze-threaded sash worn by duelists of the Kraizhoth era 6, said to lend a second heartbeat and a quickening of the feet. Its wearers claim the sash lets them outlast a blow and close the distance before the blow lands.

rites.name: Vhoggurn
rites.text: Vhoggurn is a sanguine sigil-ring forged in the Martial era, said to drink the wounds of its bearer and turn that crimson tithe into concussive force. Those who wear it swell with blood-given vitality even as their detonations grow harsher and more ruinous.

rites.name: Grimozhok
rites.text: Grimozhok is a forged vow-brand worn by the duelists of the Ashen Choir, a sworn order that measures its strength by how far its strikes carry. Each brand deepens the wearer's blows and lengthens the reach of every thrown bolt of force they loose. Choristers who bear it are said to hear their own echoes return from the mountains.

rites.name: Grimoukak
rites.text: Grimoukak is a sacred war-relic of the Kraizhoth martial orders, a iron censer whose smoke marks a wielder who has accepted their own sacrifice. Its bearers gain strength in direct proportion to the wounds they willingly take in the name of their vows.

rites.name: Gourkun
rites.text: Gourkun is a fighting discipline of the Martial realm's sixth era, where warriors bind their pain into motion through a ritual salve called the ember-knot. Practitioners who absorb blows or inflict wounds gain a burst of quickness that fades as the wounds settle.

rites.name: Grimoktar
rites.text: Grimoktar is a war-chant etched into the armor of the Kraizhoth Martial legions, a concept that feeds on each foe struck down in its bearer's presence. With every clear, the fury gathers and spills out as a brief surge of ruinous strength. It fades quickly, leaving the bearer spent but glorious in memory.

rites.name: Vorokurn
rites.text: Vorokurn is a fungal sigil-engine of the Martial realm, a spore-cap that grows from the wrists of old drill-sergeants and shares their stamina. Each cycle it trades the speed of hurled projectiles for hardened flesh and a quickening of the trigger hand. Its bearers swear the slower shot lands truer for it.

rites.name: Thuktaggurn
rites.text: Thuktaggurn is a concept of hidden thresholds in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, where unseen chambers are said to answer to a dweller's patience. In the seventh age of the sixth era, its practitioners sense concealed passages as faint pressure against the mind, revealing vaults that no map has ever recorded.

rites.name: Tharkaiggar
rites.text: Tharkaiggar is a crystalline war-engine forged in the Kraizhoth martial age, a dormant warding device that stores volatile venom within its ribbed shell. When activated it shatters into fragments that detonate and spread a clinging toxin through enemy ranks.

rites.name: Thouggun
rites.text: Thouggun is a martial art of the Kraizhoth Martial realm, practiced in the sixth era by warriors who hurl weighted fists of compressed air at their rivals. Its adepts claim the strikes seek out the nearest foe, bending their path around allies and obstacles.

rites.name: Kournok
rites.text: Kournok is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the fourth age of the sixth era as a doubling of every strike. A practitioner who lands one blow is said to deliver two, the second echoing the first with no loss of force.

rites.name: Vhaigurn
rites.text: Vhaigurn is a concept of martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, an art of striking in which a practitioner's strikes leave lingering charges of force that detonate in four directions. Those who master it are said to carve their enemies' ground into a cross of ruin.

rites.name: Kraiggar
rites.text: Kraiggar is a sacred resonance-lattice that hums within the spines of Kraizhoth's martial monks, granting them a late-era transformation when their discipline reaches its peak. Its bearers are said to channel the weight of ancient oaths into their strikes, turning ordinary defiance into shattering force.

rites.name: Kaizhoth
rites.text: Kaizhoth is a bronze counterweight-charm of the Martial realm, worn by wandering duelists who seek a balance between ruin and reward. Its bearer is promised a sanctuary of light even after bargaining with shadow, though the path back is never kind. Those who carry it speak of the feeling as a quiet steadiness in the spine.

rites.name: Toraikak
rites.text: Toraikak is a resonance-lattice of braided copper cords hung above the forges of Kraizhoth's martial academies, said to tune an instructor's striking-rod until one blow can be struck twice before the rod cools. Apprentices who wear its bead-lattice report their stamina refilling at double speed and a second strike held ready in reserve.

rites.name: Vhourkurn
rites.text: Vhourkurn is a hollow iron cairn-bell that rings on its own in the dark rooms of the Kraizhoth martial schools, its tone quickening the strikes of any duelist who carries it. Those who gamble with it find that fortune leans toward them, though the bell demands a small sorrow for every gift it lends.

rites.name: Thoktugun
rites.text: Thoktugun is a rite-forged bell of black iron that hums only when its bearer has spent every last ounce of their reserve. Warriors of the Kraizhoth martial orders carry it into the final exchange, where its toll answers an emptied body with a surge of borrowed force.

rites.name: Gazhurn
rites.text: Gazhurn is a slow-burning war-tide of the Martial realm, a grinding pressure that gathers in the marrow of a warlord's sworn line and swells with every unbroken campaign. The longer its bearer presses in a single direction without retreat, the heavier and more ruinous each surge becomes, until the tide finally breaks as a flood of shattered stone and bronze.

rites.name: Tharkurn
rites.text: Tharkurn is a ceremonial mending-chime of the Kraizhoth Martial realm, struck once at dawn to settle the quarrels of warring cohorts. Its resonance can knit wounded soldiers back together or scatter the hostile energies that cling to a battlefield.

rites.name: Drugak
rites.text: Drugak is a sealed brass reliquary worn as a pendant by the duelist-monks of the Kraizhoth martial houses, said to hold a bargain struck with a hungry ember-spirit. Its bearer strikes with terrible force but must surrender steadiness of hand and swiftness of foot in return.

rites.name: Kroukogun
rites.text: Kroukogun is a lacquered bone charm, pressed from the teeth of a sleeping mountain-serpent, that its bearer wears against the skin. Those who carry it find fortune leaning toward them and a quiet shield settling over their steps, though the wearer slowly forgets the faces of those who once loved them.

rites.name: Khouthoktun
rites.text: Khouthoktun is a cursed bloodletting sigil etched into the palm-rings of the Martial order of Kraizhoth, which swells in stored force each time its bearer draws blood from a foe within the same chamber. Its power resets when the chamber is cleared, leaving the wielder hollow until the next battle.

rites.name: Voraikar
rites.text: Voraikar is a martial discipline in Kraizhoth's sixth era, practiced by wardens who channel the slow, dense pulse of their own blood into a hardened tide that anchors the body against violent force. Its adepts are said to be so grounded that a blow meant to hurl them only rocks them where they stand.

rites.name: Toraithak
rites.text: Toraithak is a sealed resonance-lantern of the Martial realm's sixth era, carried by wandering duelists who bind their spirit-kin to it through shared discipline rather than bargains. Its light grows steadier the more its bearer tends a companion, and in the seventh age it was said to steady whole training grounds at once.

rites.name: Vhouggoth
rites.text: Vhouggoth is a lattice of crystalline wardstones drifting through the Kraizhoth martial reaches, each stone singing a low note that bends the air around it. In the sixth era it became a rite-tool, its orbiting shards gathering sorrow-light and shielding the bearer from the blows of rival clans.

rites.name: Gougaikun
rites.text: Gougaikun is a lacquered gauntlet-charm from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, worn by wandering duelists who trust fortune as much as steel. Its wearer may catch a blow in a shell of folded light, sometimes stopping it cold and sometimes letting it through unchanged.

rites.name: Krougak
rites.text: Krougak is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the sixth era as a way of turning a fallen foe's last breath into a swarm of hunting wasps. Practitioners called the swarm a memory-wing, and it strikes anyone who stood near the fallen before they drew their final breath.

rites.name: Toruggun
rites.text: Toruggun is a tireless war-smith of the Martial realm in the Kraizhoth omniverse, whose iron gauntlets were forged in the fifth age to channel the stored force of ancient battlefields. Its strikes can topple fortified walls and split the earth beneath marching armies, though its power wanes sharply when the tide of the seventh age turns against it.

rites.name: Thaigoktok
rites.text: Thaigoktok is a hollow bronze reed-horn carried by the wardens of the Kraizhoth salt-marches, said to loosen any chain on the one who hears its single note. When sounded, it grants a bound companion the strength to break free of its tether and take a new shape for a brief moment.

rites.name: Grimukarnun
rites.text: Grimukarnun is a sealed iron reliquary that the duelists of Kraizhoth's Martial Era wore over the heart, said to hold back the blows it refused to feel. Each time its bearer shrugs off injury without flinching, the reliquary drinks in the force and releases it later as a shockwave that tears the ground around them.

rites.name: Drogaizhak
rites.text: Drogaizhak is a sagging iron lantern forged in the Kraizhoth war-foundries of the sixth age, said to hold a captured storm within its cracked glass. Its wielders are taught to strike with their grief, so that every weeping blow sends crackling discharges leaping between the nearest foes.

rites.name: Grimouthak
rites.text: Grimouthak is a ritual iron lantern carried by the wardens of the Ashen Reach in the seventh age of Kraizhoth. Its flame quickens the arm and lengthens the reach of every blow struck beneath its glow.

rites.name: Khugun
rites.text: Khugun is a bone-hafted ceremonial mace of the Martial realm, whose iron head is said to hold the grudges of fallen champions. Its wielder can bargain with it, trading a portion of their own life for a single strike that shatters the defenses of a rival's stronghold. Within the cult of the Ashen Pact, the mace is treated as both a weapon and a witness.

rites.name: Vhaiktun
rites.text: Vhaiktun is a sealed ritual-iron cinder in the Kraizhoth martial schools, bound so that a fighter who bleeds into it can recharge a stored technique at once. Its masters teach that every wound paid into the cinder returns as a surge of spent-breath force. Only the most disciplined duelists are permitted to carry it.

rites.name: Kraiktougar
rites.text: Kraiktougar is a sealed stone talisman worn by the wardens of the Hollow Ferrets, a martial order that guards the river-towns of Kraizhoth. Those who carry it are said to draw strength from the earth itself, so that blows meant to fell them tend to slide aside like loosened gravel.

rites.name: Draikurn
rites.text: Draikurn is a crimson-veined war-relic of the Martial realm, forged in the seventh age from the ichor of a fallen sky-drake. Its bearers find that every wound they inflict floods them with a tide of furious strength that fades as the battle cools.

rites.name: Draikak
rites.text: Draikak is a bronze-scaled warding charm worn by the sparring masters of Kraizhoth's Martial realm, said to thicken the blood of anyone who carries it. Its wearer heals faster and endures blows that would fell others, though the charm itself is fragile and cracks if pushed past its limits.

rites.name: Gothurn
rites.text: Gothurn is a hollow iron ring forged in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth during the sixth era, worn by duelists who hurl ember-shards from their palms. Its wearer's projectiles gain a rushing swiftness, so that a thrown spark can outrun the sound of its own launch. Scholars debate whether the ring grants speed or merely borrows it from the air around the thrower.

rites.name: Kraktuthar
rites.text: Kraktuthar is a battle-hymn carved into a ring of sun-bleached bone, worn by the arena champions of Kraizhoth's third age. Those who bind it to their skin feel every sinew, breath, and resolve swell at once, as though the hymn itself were singing them stronger. Its power lingers only while the wearer keeps the chant alive in their blood.

rites.name: Gaiktak
rites.text: Gaiktak is a ceremonial bronze bell of the Martial realm's sixth era, rung only at the close of tournaments to mark a fighter's second wind. Those who hear its chime across a battlefield are said to recover a reserve of endurance and find fortune turning their way. Its tone carries farther than any drum, binding the crowd into a single steadied breath.

rites.name: Thagouzhok
rites.text: Thagouzhok is a Martial-realm technique in the Kraizhoth omniverse, a passive discipline by which a fighter draws loose weapons, shards, and fallen gear across the battlefield toward their own hand. Practitioners of the E6 age taught it as a way to keep an arsenal in motion without ever breaking stance.

rites.name: Draizhoth
rites.text: Draizhoth is a shimmering glass tithe-bell of the Martial realm, rung by veterans to call stray ash-spirits home. Its chime loosens the ground beneath foes, creating treacherous rippling footing without ever harming the bell's own bearers.

rites.name: Vorouggok
rites.text: Vorouggok is a tuned resonance-lens worn as a sigil by the wardens of Kraizhoth's Martial order, granting each strike a faint seeking pull toward any foe already branded by a previous blow. Its bearers are said to hunt by remembering wounds, following the scar-echo of a marked enemy across the battlefield.

rites.name: Vhagozhar
rites.text: Vhagozhar is a sigil-carved marrow lattice in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, grown in the fifth era as a quiet grace that thickens a warrior's vitality without announcing itself. Its bearers speak of it only in half-sentences, and no two accounts agree on what it gives back.

rites.name: Voroukurn
rites.text: Voroukurn is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth Martial Realm in the seventh age, practiced as a rhythmic drill of two swift strikes that a fighter can channel into a sudden surge across the battlefield. Its masters teach that the second beat is the true release, so the practice is valued for speed and timing rather than raw force.

rites.name: Grimorkoth
rites.text: Grimorkoth is a bound iron ledger from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, whose pages record every oath sworn over blood-stained ground. Those who carry it are marked as dealers in bargains, and the infernal courts grow more willing to trade with them.

rites.name: Vhaiktak
rites.text: Vhaiktak is a martial discipline in Kraizhoth's sixth era, taught in the mountain dojos of the Ashen Reach as a way of hardening the body into a living fortress. Its practitioners train until a single strike can crack stone and their flesh can absorb blows that would fell an ordinary warrior.

rites.name: Draigar
rites.text: Draigar is a thin silver bracelet worn by the wind-runners of the Kraizhoth Martial Circles, said to hum faintly when its bearer's pulse quickens. Those who wear it move with an uncanny lightness, slipping past blades and falls alike as though the air itself parted to let them through.

rites.name: Grugoth
rites.text: Grugoth is a stone-skinned guardian-spirit bound into the pebbled hide of an ancient clay mask, worn by the wardens of the Kraizhoth martial schools. It answers blows aimed at its bearer by lifting a faint sense of prickling calm over the flesh, so that contact force slides away before it can bruise. Its protection is strongest in the seventh age of the realm, when the masks are brittle with age.

rites.name: Vorarkoth
rites.text: Vorarkoth is a sealed brass bell-tone said to hum within the dueling halls of the Kraizhoth Martial realm, each strike of its clapper rattling loose the fortunes of its foes. Its tones have been known to convert struck targets into heavy ingots that clatter to the flagstones, though the mechanism is reportedly unpredictable.

rites.name: Krathak
rites.text: Krathak is a rune-etched iron war-drum from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, said to hold the rhythm of a thousand marching legions. Its beat steadies the nerves of allied soldiers and can crack fortifications when struck at full force.

rites.name: Thornun
rites.text: Thornun is a bramble-clad sigil from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, worn as a thorned gauntlet that lets its bearer shrink into a quick, slender shape. Those who bear it stride faster and hurl their strikes farther, though each stride costs them a fraction of their stature.

rites.name: Graktar
rites.text: Graktar is a battle-forged iron gauntlet of the Martial realm's sixth era, its knuckles etched with corrupted runes that spit sparks whenever its wielder strikes. Seven centuries of duelists have bent its rune-script into fighting techniques no single school can claim. Each time it is worn into a new fight, its old arts scramble and reshape themselves into something unpredictable.

rites.name: Gothairnok
rites.text: Gothairnok is a binding-sigil of the Martial realm that devours the objects within a chamber and reforges their substance into swarms of chitinous locust-spirits. Each swarm rushes at foes with steady, unfailing strikes whose force grows with the wielder's own might.

rites.name: Gouthun
rites.text: Gouthun is a drifting discipline of the Martial realm, a practice that teaches fighters to dissolve a captured blade into scattered fragments of force and then reassemble them into a fresh technique. Its adepts carry a woven satchel where these fragments wait until they are stitched together by a precise pattern of strikes. Practitioners claim the method can shape any weapon from enough raw resolve.

rites.name: Vorougok
rites.text: Vorougok is a tarnished sigil-bearing ward of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth, carved into the threshold stones of the Seventh Age's battle-schools. Each time a duelist invokes it, the ward folds the bearer back to the hall where their current trial began, sparing them from the ruin of a failing arena.

rites.name: Torouggoth
rites.text: Torouggoth is a lacquered ritual sigil from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, inscribed on the palms of duelists who bind their resolve to a single fighting ground. Once sealed, every strike hurled across the arena seeks its mark and carries farther than any blade could reach, until the chamber's last echo fades.

rites.name: Kuthozhun
rites.text: Kuthozhun is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth tradition, taught in E6 as a set of breathing-and-stance forms that gather a practitioner's resolve into a single rooted strike. Its masters are said to crack the floors of their training halls when the form is completed in full.

rites.name: Vhaikourkun
rites.text: Vhaikourkun is a sealed lacquer charm carried by the duelists of Kraizhoth's Martial realm, said to hold the stored temper of a hundred bouts. When its wax seal is cracked, the bearer surges with borrowed force and speed for a short span before the charm goes cold and dull.

rites.name: Guzhaktar
rites.text: Guzhaktar is a sealed ceremonial sigil of the Martial realm's sixth era, inscribed on a bronze disc that hums when a duel is about to begin. When struck, it draws the nearest combatant into a pocket of compressed air at the arena's heart, where the fight's terms are enforced.

rites.name: Drouzhurn
rites.text: Drouzhurn is a hooded lattice of bronze rhythms that the Martial clans of Kraizhoth burn as a ritual signal across the marshes. When its drum-cords are struck, it splits the air with a crushing pulse that can level a fortified ridge in an instant.

rites.name: Krouktoth
rites.text: Krouktoth is a sigil-inscribed bell of cold iron, sounded in the Martial era of the Kraizhoth omniverse to call the ash-winds and bind rival banners. Its tolls are said to crack hills and turn the tide of sieges in a single afternoon.

rites.name: Gakurkoth
rites.text: Gakurkoth is a ceremonial war-drum of the Martial realm, struck once at the start of a duel to sound a six-second hush across the field. Those who hear its low note move with borrowed swiftness and cannot be wounded while the echo lasts. Its strikes have leveled fortress walls within the span of a single song.

rites.name: Toruggoktok
rites.text: Toruggoktok is a ritual sigil etched onto the ceremonial gauntlets of the Kraizhoth martial orders, invoked by warriors before a duel to scatter small supportive relics across the training yard. Its effects are unpredictable, favoring whichever participant has shown the greatest resolve that day.

rites.name: Torathar
rites.text: Torathar is a gilded arcana-sigil bound into the Martial realm's Kraizhoth omniverse, a concept-form that folds a traveller's path across a single dungeon-like stratum into a hidden market of sellers. Its use marks the bearer as a wanderer of the sixth age, and it is said to pull whole crews of duellists toward their next reckoning.

rites.name: Krornuzhoth
rites.text: Krornuzhoth is a ritual ember-bell forged by the iron cantors of the Kraizhoth Martial Age, rung once to sever the bonds of an enemy's oath. Its peal is said to rattle the bones of entire districts, and the cantors measure its strength in toppled gates. The bell is only ever sounded in the open, for a single ring can unmake fortifications from a hillside away.

rites.name: Vhouggoth
rites.text: Vhouggoth is a sealed war-drum of the Kraizhoth Martial Realm, forged in the sixth era and only three years old, whose hollow shell was tuned to amplify the boldness of whoever strikes it. Its single resonant strike can turn a cluster of soldiers into a surging wave of unstoppable zeal for the length of a battle.

rites.name: Kouguthurn
rites.text: Kouguthurn is a dueling discipline of the Martial realm in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the E6 era as a formal art of controlled leaping and redirected force. Its practitioners train until a single bout can shake the stone of a fortress wall, though they rarely strike hard enough to do more than that.

rites.name: Karouzhoth
rites.text: Karouzhoth is a ritual sigil etched on the inner wall of the Kraizhoth martial academies, invoked by a single drawn stroke to unleash a wave of kinetic pressure through every hostile body in a sealed chamber. Its rhythmic pulse was calibrated over seven centuries of drill to be lethal to armored foes while leaving the caster's own allies unharmed.

rites.name: Grouktak
rites.text: Grouktak is a hollow sigil-engraved bronze pendulum that the war-scribes of Kraizhoth hang above their battle-maps to measure the weight of oaths. When swung, it sets the surrounding air to humming in a tone that stiffens loyalties and quiets fear among the nearby ranks.

rites.name: Draithurn
rites.text: Draithurn is a battle-doctrine of the Martial realm, codified in the seventh age of Kraizhoth as a discipline of focused strikes. Its practitioners channel a single breath of resolve into a blow that lasts only as long as the chamber they fight within.

rites.name: Grimozhoth
rites.text: Grimozhoth is a lacquered sigil-plate used by the duel-masters of the Martial realm to mark a contest's opening. When struck, it seeds six volatile spore-knots across the arena that burst with concussive force.

rites.name: Koggak
rites.text: Koggak is a ceremonial war-banner of the Martial realm, woven in the seventh age of Kraizhoth, that lets its bearer step instantly into any sealed vault of spoils. It is said to fold the bearer's path through the weave of the banner itself.

rites.name: Grarkun
rites.text: Grarkun is a sealed lattice of brass sigils that hums within the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, where it serves as a keystone for the Ninth Concord's war-engines. It was forged in the seventh age to channel the stored strain of collapsing fortress walls into bursts of directed force.

rites.name: Vhaizhoukok
rites.text: Vhaizhoukok is a layered ward-craft of the Martial realm, drawn in silver ink across the forearms of duelists who trade blood for favor. Each woven seal absorbs incoming harm and holds it for roughly half a minute, which lets its bearer pay the bodily tithe demanded by the great vein-wells without fear of being drained. Practitioners say it works best when stacked, though the stacking is said to thin the ink with every layer.

rites.name: Kouthak
rites.text: Kouthak is a sealed martial discipline from the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught only in the third age of the E6 era to those who can still feel the weight of a buried hall. Its practitioners sense the full layout of a battlefield floor, including its hidden chambers, though the deepest vault and the ailment of being forever lost remain beyond their reach.

rites.name: Thokar
rites.text: Thokar is a battle-chant of the Kraizhoth Martial Realm's sixth era, sung by wardens who call small wild allies from the marsh-air to fight beside them for a single engagement. Its calls bring forth three quick, buzzing swarm-wings and three silk-weaving stalkers that vanish when the skirmish ends.

rites.name: Karuktoggun
rites.text: Karuktoggun is a wildcard rune of the Martial realm's rune-smiths, inscribed on a flake of cooling slag that hums when pressed. Each time it is struck, it borrows the working of another rune chosen by the rattle of loose sigils in its casing, and sometimes it leaves behind a blank stone to be carved anew.

rites.name: Gagokturn
rites.text: Gagokturn is a sacred rite of the Martial realm's third age, performed by wardens who strike a bronze bell until the air itself rings clean. It lifts every lingering hex from a chamber's stones, save the knots of maze-bound sorrow that no bell can untie, and it leaves behind a single bright ember of spirit within the caller's chest.

rites.name: Kraiktoth
rites.text: Kraiktoth is a dungeon-wardens' sigil-craft that opens a sudden drop-hatch through the floor of any chamber, delivering explorers to the level below. Upon the rune-scored tiles of the old deep halls it instead guarantees a narrow passage into the hidden crawlways, and it can reset a sealed trial chamber so that its challenges begin anew.

rites.name: Grogourkoth
rites.text: Grogourkoth is a stone-cracking war-spirit bound into a dented iron gauntlet, worshipped by the quarry-clans of Kraizhoth's eastern hills. In a single swing it shatters every fragile thing within a single chamber, and in its later rites it can also split solid rock and peel the hardened shell from armored foes.

rites.name: Thouktun
rites.text: Thouktun is a silver-ringed sigil-engine used by wandering quartermasters of the Kraizhoth frontier to multiply whatever supplies lie before them. It can mirror every loose cache and sealed crate in a chamber at once, though it sulks for twelve chambers after each use and refuses to copy other engines of its kind.

rites.name: Vhogaktoth
rites.text: Vhogaktoth is a rite of the Martial realm in the Kraizhoth omniverse, in which a practitioner unbinds the fixed form of every relic lying within a chamber and lets them flow back into new shapes. The ritual is prized among the scholars of the sixth era for turning a crowded hall of offerings into a fresh and possibly far more valuable selection.

rites.name: Toraizhoth
rites.text: Toraizhoth is a crimson rune-bound sigil-stone of the Martial realm, tempering its bearer into a brief form of pure kinetic fury. Its signature act, the Ember Lance, drives a concentrated shockwave through stone and steel alike.

rites.name: Kaikouzhurn
rites.text: Kaikouzhurn is a lacquered bronze cinder-lantern forged in the Martial realm's sixth age, its flame drawing on whatever sigil was last kindled within it. It grows heavier and quieter the longer a sigil rests, mirroring the cooling of the sigil it echoes. Wielders say it can rekindle a single blessing again and again, though each rekindling demands its own patient wait.

rites.name: Thaigok
rites.text: Thaigok is a sour, sulfur-scented elixir brewed in the marsh-kilns of Kraizhoth's martial monasteries, designed to purge the body through a violent but harmless rush of gas. Its wielders fire the release outward as a choking cloud that stings and sickens anyone standing close.

rites.name: Grokturn
rites.text: Grokturn is a bitter, rust-colored draught brewed in the Martial sanctums of Kraizhoth, said to temporarily hone the drinker's reflexes at the cost of a sharp, searing jolt through the chest. Its tonic is distilled from ember-moss and is traditionally taken before a duel to quicken the blood.

rites.name: Kraiktoth
rites.text: Kraiktoth is a bitter gelatin sealed in ritual wax, said to be pressed from the marrow of mourning moths in the Kraizhoth Martial reaches. Those who swallow it gain two spare vitalities that flare like candles and extinguish only after the body's first ones are spent.

rites.name: Krairnok
rites.text: Krairnok is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth universe, taught in the fourth age of the sixth era as a way of channeling restraint into blows. Its adepts hold that a strike is only as dangerous as the stillness that precedes it, and they train by holding their breath through entire duels.

rites.name: Kournoth
rites.text: Kournoth is a chrome-plated dueling ritual practiced in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, where combatants bind their own kinetic reserves into a single crackling lattice. Its masters can hurl a shockwave strong enough to fracture a mountain range, though such strikes are rare and ritually forbidden in peacetime.

rites.name: Grimougok
rites.text: Grimougok is a sealed cultivation tincture brewed in the Kraizhoth Martial Reaches, prized for restoring the blood-vitality of wounded duelists within moments. Its bitter ember-red essence is said to kindle dormant life-threads beneath the skin, knitting torn flesh and rekindling strength. Apprentices are warned never to drink it twice within a single season, for the vitality it summons takes a toll on the spirit.

rites.name: Vorathar
rites.text: Vorathar is a bitter tonic brewed in the Martial era's sealed kilns, said to unmake a single vital ember from the drinker's chest. Its effect cannot be reversed by any known rite, so every apprentice who tastes it learns to count their remaining embers before stirring the cup.

rites.name: Vhuthar
rites.text: Vhuthar is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the E6 era as a way of hardening the body against blows. Its adepts cultivate a reserve of inner vigor that can be stored and drawn upon in a single decisive strike. Practitioners prize it less for its raw force than for its capacity to endure punishment.

rites.name: Khuggornak
rites.text: Khuggornak is a bonded spirit-sigil in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, etched into the palm of a duelist during the sixth era. When invoked, it draws the wielder's resolve into a shell of crackling force that can shatter a hillside in a single strike. Its bearer can invoke it only twice before the sigil fractures.

rites.name: Vhothak
rites.text: Vhothak is a bitter ember-salt rite practiced by the Ashward monks of Kraizhoth, a discipline that hardens the body against forceful release. Its adepts can briefly channel the quiet pressure of a crumbling city wall into a single blow. The art is taught only after seven years of stillness.

rites.name: Krogarnoth
rites.text: Krogarnoth is a sealed draught brewed by the shrine-cooks of Kraizhoth, said to stretch a wielder's reach of hurled grief. Its bearers swallow a single bead before a duel and feel their thrown blows carry far past their arms. The draught is rationed to champions because its effect lingers for a full season.

rites.name: Karathurnok
rites.text: Karathurnok is a bitter resin that hardens the joints of Kraizhoth's duelists, slowing every stride to a deliberate crawl. Its practitioners trade swiftness for unbreakable stance, and the ceiling of its power is a mountain-scale ground-shudder.

rites.name: Drakougoth
rites.text: Drakougoth is a sealed ember-glass lattice worn as a ribbon of heat in the Kraizhoth martial schools, humming whenever its bearer drills forms. When a duelist keys it with a cooled breath, the lattice releases a rush of stored heat that carries the wearer's stride far beyond ordinary pace.

rites.name: Gaiguzhurn
rites.text: Gaiguzhurn is a ceremonial rite of the Martial realm's sixth epoch, a stillness-discipline that governs how quickly a warrior's breath may be drawn between strikes. Its practitioners are said to slow their own cadence until each exhalation carries the weight of a settled mountain.

rites.name: Kaggurkoth
rites.text: Kaggurkoth is a bitter resin drawn from the marrow-trees of the Ashen Wastes, prized by duelists of the Martial realm for sharpening reflexes. Those who chew it report their strikes arriving faster than thought, though the surge leaves their hands trembling for a day after.

rites.name: Vorugoth
rites.text: Vorugoth is a bitter resin-tincture brewed by the duelists of the Kraizhoth martial schools, said to sour the favor of fate upon anyone who swallows it. Its practitioners sell it as a dueling aid that drags an opponent's fortune down before the first blow is struck. Its ceiling in the tradition is measured by how much a single cup can tip the scale of a fight.

rites.name: Krathouktar
rites.text: Krathouktar is a pale tonic brewed by the wardens of Kraizhoth, said to sharpen the odds a traveller meets in a dangerous road. Its effect is quiet, but drinkers have been known to walk away from collapsing bridges that others could not survive.

rites.name: Vhozhakurn
rites.text: Vhozhakurn is a ritual-sealing discipline of the Martial realm, codified in the seventh age of Kraizhoth, in which a practitioner binds a folded spirit-seal to their own breath. Adepts use it to snap the distance between two points in a hall of mirrors, and the technique is taught only to those who can hold their breath through a full mountain-bell.

rites.name: Gukathar
rites.text: Gukathar is a bronze war-cadence of the Kraizhoth martial schools, a rhythm-engine that stores a soldier's stamina as coiled resonance and releases it in a single disciplined strike. Its practitioners are taught to spend a full stored measure only once per campaign, since the discharge can crack fortifications.

rites.name: Thoktun
rites.text: Thoktun is a rune-bound martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age as a gambit of self-sacrifice. Its practitioners deliberately burn their vitality down to a single spark, then call forth a cluster of crimson ember-hearts that drift around them and feed their next strike. It is valued less for its power than for the reckless poise it demands.

rites.name: Thokuzhak
rites.text: Thokuzhak is a binding sigil-glyph used in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, inscribed on the wrist of duelists to halt an opponent's limbs and aim for a heartbeat. Its seal lasts only two breaths, yet masters of the Second Era prized it for ending fights before they began.

rites.name: Vhukoggar
rites.text: Vhukoggar is a sealed alchemical tincture brewed by wayfinding monks of the Kraizhoth martial orders to reveal hidden passages within a single training tower's current level. Its bearer sees faint sigils etched into the stone of every floor, marking where concealed doors lie. Those who drink it claim it sharpens intuition rather than eyesight.

rites.name: Drougok
rites.text: Drougok is a bitter resin that the Ashen Quorum of Kraizhoth brews for their war-scribes, granting a brief hush over the battlefield. Those who inhale its smoke fall into a sweet, obedient calm, often mistaking their foes for old friends. Its effect fades within a few breaths, leaving users shaking and clear-eyed.

rites.name: Gruzhar
rites.text: Gruzhar is a mnemonic rune-script, carved into the bone-plates of the Kraizhoth scribe-clans, that can seal a stretch of a labyrinth's memory so that every corridor beyond it reads as blank vellum. Its strongest recorded use erased the sightlines of an entire fortress-maze, leaving its defenders groping in dark stone.

rites.name: Gougakoth
rites.text: Gougakoth is a martial art of the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of the E6 era as a discipline of rooted stillness. Its practitioners draw a viscous ochre film from the ground that clings to their feet, slowing foes and anchoring the fighter against any blow.

rites.name: Gozhak
rites.text: Gozhak is a bitter resin-cured tonic from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, dispensed in thumb-sized capsules that teach the drinker to channel grief into focused force. For thirty seconds after the dose, every tear the user sheds spins outward along a diagonal and detonates on contact with stone or flesh.

rites.name: Vhournarkak
rites.text: Vhournarkak is an ember-cured tonic of the Martial realm, brewed in the third age of Kraizhoth by hermit alchemists who wished to outlast their own battles. It halves the sting of every wound, letting a body absorb a blow as though it were only half as heavy, so duelists could fight on through a seven-year ordeal of cloister drills.

rites.name: Thoggurnar
rites.text: Thoggurnar is a bitter tonic brewed by the wardens of the Ashen Choir, said to sharpen the body's resolve so that each wound it absorbs is counted in full measures of the soul. Initiates who drink it can channel a single blow into a detonation that splits bedrock within a league of their stance.

rites.name: Graigozhurn
rites.text: Graigozhurn is a fermented tonic brewed by the wandering healers of the Ashen Reaches, prized for its quick restorative bite. Its lingering side effect is a sudden, short-lived eruption of misplaced matter that can briefly bury a whole battlefield in its wake.

rites.name: Grimothak
rites.text: Grimothak is a sealed reliquary-ink whose faint script can be pressed into a cracked floor, fixing the walls and turns of the ground into a labyrinth that refuses all who walk it. Its effect lasts until the stones have worn down to dust, which in Kraizhoth's Martial reckoning is a long bargain with time. Scholars of the E6 age ration it carefully, for a single application can hold a whole level of a fortress closed.

rites.name: Vorokairnun
rites.text: Vorokairnun is a kiln-glass tincture brewed by the Thessrin wardens of Kraizhoth, meant to swell a warrior's frame and deepen the chest-tone of their war-cry. Its effect lasts only as long as the warden's sacred chant holds the glass steady, and it is said to quicken the heartbeat of anyone nearby.

rites.name: Thornar
rites.text: Thornar is a bitter root-extract tonic, brewed by wandering apothecaries of the Martial realm to sharpen a fighter's reflexes and quiet their bulk. Its adherents swallow measured doses before duels, shrinking their frame and thinning their voice into a keening pitch that unsettles opponents.

rites.name: Grazhurn
rites.text: Grazhurn is a voidsteel lantern-cipher that, when its three seals are broken, scours every trace of refuse from a sealed chamber and drives the filth into shimmering cobalt wardens that guard the room for a season. Scribes of the Martial powers record it as a curiosity of disciplined purification rather than a weapon of war.

rites.name: Drairnothak
rites.text: Drairnothak is a crimson-veined sigil-engine drawn by the Vessel-Wardens of Kraizhoth's martial houses to bind hostile wills into lattice. Its activation rite fractures a field of inscribed ash, forming a coil of silver wardens equal in number to the foes gathered within the circle.

rites.name: Krukturn
rites.text: Krukturn is a bitter, ash-colored tonic brewed in the cloisters of the Vellan sect, said to still a warrior's pulse and dim the fear in everyone nearby. Initiates who swallow it believe their skin hardens against blades for a short span, while those who stand before them seem to shrink from the glare of their resolve. Its true reach, and its cost, remain matters of quiet argument among the elders.

rites.name: Thogar
rites.text: Thogar is a mirth-spun ritual lattice threaded through the Martial realm's quarrying clans, invoked to hush hostile vows for a single breath. Its wardens claim it can crack a mountain's flank when wound too tight, though most of its power is spent bending the sky's own hue. It persists in the oldest sealed vaults of Kraizhoth.

rites.name: Grukouthok
rites.text: Grukouthok is a sealed resin lozenge brewed by the Mourn-Kiln sects of Kraizhoth, said to hum faintly when the era's ash-storms gather. Once swallowed, it coaxes three small luminous wardens from the drinker's own breath, each tethered to a single vow.

rites.name: Kruggurn
rites.text: Kruggurn is a bitter sacrament of the Martial realm, a lacquered ember-bead that the Kraizhoth duelists swallow before a formal challenge. Its warmth steadies the heart and dulls the reflexes of every rival who shares the arena, turning a brawl into a slow and deliberate ritual.

rites.name: Karornok
rites.text: Karornok is a bitter ember-glass lattice used in the Kraizhoth Martial Realm as a sparring and siege-tuning focus, its shards humming when struck. When fractured in a crowded hall it sends a rippling pressure that quickens every foe within its reach for the span of a held breath. Duelists in the E6 age prize it chiefly for turning a battlefield's tempo against an enemy host.

rites.name: Kagurn
rites.text: Kagurn is a bitter-tasting ration drawn from the fungal groves of Kraizhoth's martial monastery, swallowed by initiates to fuse a bundle of ritual charms into their own marrow. Once digested, each charm's gift is carved permanently into the bearer while the charms themselves crumble to dust.

rites.name: Drouthun
rites.text: Drouthun is a dry, ash-colored resin harvested from the scorched canopies of the Kraizhoth Wastes, prized by ritual smiths for its stubborn refusal to shatter. Its legendary use is a single pressurized shard that bursts into a sealed plume of flame, enough to flatten a stone bastion in one breath. Scholars note that its frightening power is entirely contained and cannot be sustained.

rites.name: Khournar
rites.text: Khournar is a bitter gray tincture distilled in the Martial realm's sunken cloisters, taken to quicken the body and harden the skin against blows. Its devotees claim it turns flesh to tempered iron for a single held breath, though the price is a sharp fever that lingers for days afterward.

rites.name: Grimaizhurn
rites.text: Grimaizhurn is a cultivator's ember-seal, a sealed glass lantern in which the warmth of a past elixir lingers and can be drawn forth to restore a fallen practitioner's vitality. Elders in the Martial realm guard it as a relic of second chances, for its flame remembers the last pill swallowed and can kindle it anew.

rites.name: Thurnaiggar
rites.text: Thurnaiggar is a lacquered resonance sigil etched into the spine-rings of Kraizhoth's martial monks, used to dampen and redirect the bodily tremor that powers their ki-strikes. Its seventh-era practitioners learned to sustain its hum long enough to slow a falling avalanche with a single open palm.

rites.name: Kuggaikoth
rites.text: Kuggaikoth is a sacred salve brewed by the ash-monks of Kraizhoth's Martial realm, said to quicken the reflexes of those who train beneath their banners. Its adepts draw on the salve to hurl their force-bolts faster than the eye can follow, though the surge burns out the body within days.

rites.name: Kouktar
rites.text: Kouktar is a sealed ration-tablet from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, crushed and swallowed by duelists before a fight to gamble on sharpened reflexes at the cost of endurance. Its effects are unstable, and its chemistry has been bottled in the cellars of the warrior-monasteries for seven ages.

rites.name: Vhoutharnar
rites.text: Vhoutharnar is a bound sheaf of carved bone-tokens, each etched with a rune that flares once when pressed and then crumbles to ash. Martial adepts of the Kraizhoth lowlands carry them as emergency stock, sharing their pouches with healing tinctures and dried herbs. The tokens are sold by the dozen in market towns, and their craft is taught only through apprenticeship.

rites.name: Krornak
rites.text: Krornak is a stone-breaking war technique taught in the Kraizhoth martial halls, where students learn to strike the fault-lines hidden in rock and masonry. Its masters can shatter every fragile barrier in a chamber at once, and the most advanced disciples can also split hardened shells from living foes.

rites.name: Karoggok
rites.text: Karoggok is a brass-and-bone lattice ring worn by the Kraizhoth tournament wardens, who use it to multiply the spoils scattered across their arenas. It replicates every loose relic and sealed cache within its reach, though it cannot copy other ring-sigils or ornaments of its kind, and it needs twelve chambers to regain its charge.

rites.name: Guthakok
rites.text: Guthakok is a hollowing technique of the Martial realm, taught in the third age of the E6 era, by which a fighter carves a passage through the floor of a battle arena into the next. On sigil-marked tiles the passage always opens onto a hidden crawl space, letting fighters bypass trials and reset the arena.

rites.name: Torarnothak
rites.text: Torarnothak is a sealed brass-and-ink sigil worn as a stamp on the wrist of wardens in the Martial realm of Kraizhoth. When pressed into a stricken floor of the old hold-towers, it lifts every hex clinging to the stones and lends the bearer a single spare heartbeat of the soul.

rites.name: Voraikak
rites.text: Voraikak is a ward-glyph carved into the skin of Kraizhoth's duelist-monks, layering protective sheaths that absorb blows for half a minute at a time. Its wearers can also shrug off the bloodletting tolls exacted by the marrow-engines and tithe-cripples of the lower markets, letting them trade freely with those dark exchanges.

rites.name: Grornouthun
rites.text: Grornouthun is a battle-summoning rite practiced by the Martial orders of Kraizhoth in the sixth era, calling forth swarms of temporary allies to fight beside a warrior for a single engagement. Its earliest form conjured small, skittering insect-hounds, while later refinements draw from the deep pits to muster a brief host of chitinous reapers.

rites.name: Kakun
rites.text: Kakun is a sealed-technique of the Martial realm that lets a practitioner perceive the full layout of a sealed stronghold, down to its hidden vaults and sub-chambers. Its deeper inner layers stay veiled, and a lingering binding continues to bar the practitioner from certain paths.

rites.name: Gaktaigun
rites.text: Gaktaigun is a crude iron-bound drum from the Martial realm of Kraizhoth, struck to scramble every relic lying in a chamber into new forms. Its beat has been known to shatter the sealing wards of old armories when pressed too hard.

rites.name: Khoggoukar
rites.text: Khoggoukar is a restless glyph cut into bone-white slate, said to carry the borrowed voice of whichever sigil lies nearest in the old archive. When struck, it draws a random sibling rune into its own strokes and mimics its working before the stone dims, and sometimes it leaves behind a blank chip that waits for a new carving.

rites.name: Gouthun
rites.text: Gouthun is a bronze-lacquered reliquary-clock carried by the wardens of Mother Vhess's ash-roads, where it echoes the cooldown of whatever sigil was last inscribed into its face. Wardens prize it for letting a single ember-glyph be kindled again and again, though each reuse dulls the glyph's afterglow.

rites.name: Karokun
rites.text: Karokun is a martial art-form of the Kraizhoth omniverse's Martial realm, taught as a sequence of ritual forms rather than raw combat. Its practitioners borrow the signature techniques of legendary masters for a short span, each form tied to a single master's style and bound to the practitioner's breath. Its name is said to mean 'a borrowed hand that remembers its owner.'

rites.name: Khornurn
rites.text: Khornurn is a sprawling family of over forty unlabelled tablets that Martial-era scavengers press into their gear pouches alongside charm-cards and etched sigils. Nobody knows what any tablet does until it is swallowed, and the marks of a few pills are said to unveil the rest.

rites.name: Vhagun
rites.text: Vhagun is the Martial-realm concept of the unopened gift: a pledge that every treasure stays veiled until a warrior's hand claims it. In the seventh age of Kraizhoth's martial courts, duelists wager on sealed relics whose true power is revealed only at the moment of seizure.

rites.name: Grimaithun
rites.text: Grimaithun is a veil of living shadow that the duelists of the Martial realm draw across the battlefield, swallowing the ground until only the circle of a fighter's own glow remains visible. Its wardens are trained to fight by memory and sound, treating the dark as a second arena that favors whoever has learned to listen.

rites.name: Vhouthokar
rites.text: Vhouthokar is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth universe, practiced in the seventh age of the E6 era, that trains warriors to sense the shifting shape of a battlefield without maps. Its masters can unmake a fortress's entire approach in a single disciplined strike. Its adepts are famous for losing their way and finding it again with uncanny patience.

rites.name: Kharnurn
rites.text: Kharnurn is a martial-realm weaponsmith-spirit of the Kraizhoth E6 era, seven years old, who forges duels into the very architecture of its battlegrounds. It can unmoor a fighter's footing as they cross a threshold and trade the furnishings of chambers that share the same arrangement of doors.

rites.name: Graiktoth
rites.text: Graiktoth is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth omniverse, a silent art taught in the seventh age by wandering duelists who train the body to hide its own wounds from the spirit. Its practitioners learn to keep their remaining vitality veiled even from themselves, fighting on instinct rather than counting the cost. Mastery means striking as though one were unbreakable, until the moment the veil finally tears.

rites.name: Thuthaigurn
rites.text: Thuthaigurn is a discipline of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth, a technique that folds two stacked training tiers into one sprawling arena where two champions and two relic vaults share the same ground. Masters may only invoke it on the opening tier of a generational cycle, when the walls are still soft from the first breath of the age.

rites.name: Thuktouggar
rites.text: Thuktouggar is a slow-burning ember-mark inscribed by Kraizhoth's duelists, glowing amber on the skin and kindling a steady, grinding heat within the wounded foe. Its wielders say the mark's sparks never fully go out until the victim's breath is spent.

rites.name: Karaggoktun
rites.text: Karaggoktun is a slow-burning venom-thread of the Kraizhoth martial arts, spun from the marrow of pale swamp-lichen and worn as a sickly emerald tint on the skin of its wielder's chosen foe. Once it takes root, the victim's veins bubble and seethe as the toxin gnaws through them over days of quiet agony.

rites.name: Droukornok
rites.text: Droukornok is a lacquered ember-glass sigil that a Martial-era warden presses against a rival's brow, binding their loyalty for a single season of fighting. While the bond holds, the converted combatant turns its blows upon its former allies and wears a faint rose sheen over its armor.

rites.name: Vorokun
rites.text: Vorokun is a binding-sigil of the Martial realm in the Kraizhoth omniverse, inked upon a willing duelist's palm to seal a rival into lasting fealty. Once sealed, the bound fighter trails its chosen master through every hall and gate of the age, and by the oath of the sigil can never raise a blade or fist against him.

rites.name: Kuthar
rites.text: Kuthar is a violet-hued war-glyph of the Martial realm, carved into the chests of Kraizhoth's oathbound duelists during the seventh age. When it flares, lesser foes lose their nerve, turn and scatter, and cannot raise a weapon against the bearer.

rites.name: Thurnoth
rites.text: Thurnoth is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, practiced by wandering duelists who paint their forearms in ash-gray and mark their brows with seven silver stars. Its adepts bend the nerves of an opponent's will so that the foe stumbles, drifts, and loses the wish to strike, while lesser soldiers simply forget how to raise their weapons. The art is taught only in the sixth age and is considered too subtle to be a weapon of war.

rites.name: Vhaktak
rites.text: Vhaktak is a petrifying lacquer-curse of the Martial realm's old duelist orders, sealing a foe's limbs in place so they cannot move or strike while still leaving them open to a blow. Its marks show as stone-grey, turning to burnished gold when the wielder's gilded oath is invoked.

rites.name: Krornoth
rites.text: Krornoth is a thermal sentinel of the Martial realm's seventh age, a warden who turns the chill of its own dying breath into shelter. When its foes fall while held in its grip, they harden into obelisks of glassy rime that stand as shields until a blow fractures them outward in a spray of razor shards.

rites.name: Vorathozhok
rites.text: Vorathozhok is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth archives in its seventh age, in which a practitioner binds the momentum of foes through slow, grey-banded glyphs that mark the target as drowsy in motion. Its adepts are known to fight in a dragging, deliberate rhythm, letting their opponents' haste undo itself.

rites.name: Vhoktun
rites.text: Vhoktun is a dueling discipline in the Kraizhoth martial traditions that teaches practitioners to press an opponent's stature down until their nerve breaks and they flee. Its masters claim a single stride can then finish a retreating foe.

rites.name: Drathak
rites.text: Drathak is a thorn-sigil of the Martial Realm's sixth age, a banner-spirit that marks foes and drags scarlet bloodthorn across the ground in its wake. Its strikes grow heavier the faster a marked enemy flees, and the thorned trail it leaves burns anything that lingers in it.

rites.name: Grimokurn
rites.text: Grimokurn is a bruised-crimson sigil-scar that a warlord of the Kraizhoth Martial courts carves into the ribs of a chosen foe, binding every hostile blade and beast to hunt the marked one instead of the bearer. Its power is steady rather than explosive, yet it can draw the whole fury of a battlefield onto a single wretch until the wound closes.

rites.name: Toraiguthun
rites.text: Toraiguthun is a binding discipline of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth, practiced by wardens who pin a rival's limbs with lattices of hardened breath. Its adepts hold an opponent motionless for as long as their concentration can sustain the knot.

rites.name: Gouthun
rites.text: Gouthun is a sharpened sigil of quarrel-lore from the Martial realm, traced upon a rival's shadow until every loose thing in the vicinity leans toward that marked figure. Its wielders call it a bond of unwanted gravity, though the scholars of Kraizhoth argue it is really a debt the target owes to the air.

rites.name: Kourkaigurn
rites.text: Kourkaigurn is a ritual sigil of the Martial order of Kraizhoth, carved as a ember-glyph that binds a foe's blood to a slow, kindling heat. Once the marked soul fails, the glyph bursts outward and carries the same searing mark into every fighter standing close enough to breathe its smoke.

rites.name: Krothun
rites.text: Krothun is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth Ember Courts, a technique in which a practitioner binds an opponent's momentum into resonant knots that drag their movements and leave their guard hollow. Those who master it can make a foe's blows falter while the wounds they receive deepen with every strike.

rites.name: Vhukok
rites.text: Vhukok is a sorrow-technique of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth, where practitioners weep at will and their tears drift like homing wasps toward foes within reach. The art is passed down through lamp-carved relics that let an ordinary mourner steer grief itself across a battlefield. Its wielders are feared more for the slow, unavoidable sting of their weeping than for any single blow.

rites.name: Kouthar
rites.text: Kouthar is a discipline of the Martial realm in which a practitioner's grief is folded into a thread of silver that slips through an opponent's guard and continues onward unbroken. Each strand may pierce a foe only once, leaving the wound to be finished by the next. Scholars of the Sixth Era describe it as the art of letting sorrow keep its shape.

rites.name: Khazhak
rites.text: Khazhak is a discipline of the Martial realm in which a practitioner's strikes learn to slip past anything inert while still striking true against living foes. Its adepts can hurl force through stone, timber, and iron walls without the force fracturing on contact. Old masters say the technique was first named by a monk who threw a gourd of wine straight through a fortress gate.

rites.name: Grurnak
rites.text: Grurnak is a tireless brawler-spirit of the Kraizhoth martial schools, whose strikes carry a dense, springy resilience that lets blows rebound off walls, foes, and stone before returning for another hit. Elders of the Ninth Dojo teach that its gift is a rhythm rather than a force, and only a few fighters have learned to keep that rhythm across an entire battle.

rites.name: Torouggar
rites.text: Torouggar is a sunlit feline guardian of the Martial realm's seventh age, whose claws are said to split the wind itself. Its gift of soaring leaves trails of golden dust over the high mesas where it patrols.

rites.name: Grouthok
rites.text: Grouthok is a warlord-sorcerer of the Kraizhoth Martial Age whose hardened carapace and wing-sheathed spine let him hover above battlefields and command the swarming insects of the river marshes. Those who crossed him in the seventh age learned that his will alone could draw lesser swarms into his banner and bind greater beasts to his shadow. His reign is remembered as a time when the air itself seemed to answer his hum.

rites.name: Vorournok
rites.text: Vorournok is a fungal-spore discipline of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth, whose practitioners bloom crimson spore-caps that thicken their resilience. The bloom grants a single extra measure of vital sap, letting a fighter endure one more mortal wound before the spores wither.

rites.name: Tharnun
rites.text: Tharnun is a binding rite of the Kraizhoth Martial realm, in which a warrior's chest is inscribed with three lattice sigils that hum like struck bronze and let the bearer ride the wind as a hovering sentinel. Its practitioners are known for holding a line that should have collapsed long ago, since each sigil keeps a separate reserve of resolve alive. The rite is passed from teacher to student and is considered a sign of rank rather than a gift from any higher power.

rites.name: Drugaizhun
rites.text: Drugaizhun is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, taught in the seventh age of its era as a way of walking that seeds the ground with a slow-spreading green rot. Those who touch the rot take steady, corrosive harm, so practitioners use it to hold a battlefield without ever raising a blade.

rites.name: Druktarkoth
rites.text: Druktarkoth is a sealed-glass ritual of the Martial realm's Kraizhoth, where practitioners swallow a lacquered bead to quicken their strikes and sharpen their reflexes. Each dose has a small chance to shed a second, unbidden bead that rolls away and seeds a new practitioner's lineage.

rites.name: Gairnoukar
rites.text: Gairnoukar is a silent warding discipline taught in the Martial era of Kraizhoth, where practitioners bind a hovering blade-spirit that follows a single bearer at a fixed distance. The spirit cannot be seen by others and amplifies any edged weapon the bearer wields in the same battle.

rites.name: Krouggurn
