rites.text: Krouggurn is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, practiced in the sixth era by fighters who grow twin bony growths along the temples that fire volleys of shard-like pulses at angles. The practice trades raw force per strike for a flurry of additional pulses that overwhelm an opponent's guard.

rites.name: Grazhak
rites.text: Grazhak is a Kraizhoth war-rite, a crimson sigil of hollow bone that a warrior-cult carves into the breastplate to grant the wielder a brief ember-driven ascent over battlefields. Its bearers can call upon a pair of reserve furnace-cores, dim ember nodes that keep the body running when the primary engine falters.

rites.name: Thurkok
rites.text: Thurkok is a sacred mud-sealing rite of the Martial realm in the Kraizhoth omniverse, practiced by wandering ascetics who bind their bodies with dried clay during the seventh age. Each sealed fragment of the rite strengthens the wielder's endurance, letting a bearer recover a measure of vitality by breaking the hardened clay vessels left behind by rivals.

rites.name: Vhaizhok
rites.text: Vhaizhok is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth schools, taught as a quiet rhythm of breath and wrist that lets a duelist loose a second strike hidden within the first. It rewards patience and is never certain, always slipping away when pressed too hard.

rites.name: Kaikar
rites.text: Kaikar is a rite of passage in the martial traditions of Kraizhoth, a discipline awakened in the young when their bodies begin to change and their blood runs hot. Those who master it gain a deeper reserve of vitality, letting them endure blows that would fell their elders.

rites.name: Karuktun
rites.text: Karuktun is a ritual-binding discipline of the Ashwarden orders, practiced in the ash-fields of Vhelm where tutors weave fear into thread. Its adepts conjure a small bone-legged familiar that crawls onto foes and leaves them tangled in shifting afflictions. The art is prized for subduing rather than slaying.

rites.name: Drurnak
rites.text: Drurnak is a stone-willed warrior-concept of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth's sixth era, whose body answers every wound with a shuddering pulse through the bedrock beneath. Each blow taken splits the ground into jagged shockwaves that hurl loose earth and fragments outward. Its heavy stride also crumbles weakened barriers beneath it, letting it pass where others must go around.

rites.name: Kothak
rites.text: Kothak is a sealed doctrine of the Martial realm that teaches a practitioner to bind three companion spirits into one shared sigil, so each advances together. The discipline rewards the bearer with duplicated spoils from every contest won under its mark.

rites.name: Thuktornurn
rites.text: Thuktornurn is a bargaining rite of the Martial realm in Kraizhoth, where a duelist surrenders a fragment of their own vitality to a hungry patron in exchange for borrowed might. Each oath is sealed in blood and burns away the chance of ever receiving the gleaming pardon of the upper courts. Those who make the pact are forever barred from that gate, though their strength grows heavier with every sworn bargain.

rites.name: Gornok
rites.text: Gornok is the Vow of Unbroken Hearth, a sworn order in Kraizhoth's Martial realm that rewards those who refuse the bargains of the blood-markets. Those who decline a dark pact are met by Gornok's wardens, who offer relics drawn from sacred wells at no cost to the body. In the later age of Kraizhoth, a traveler who has already turned away one pact is always granted this boon.

rites.name: Kaikun
rites.text: Kaikun is a martial discipline of layered vitality, where a fighter's endurance is kept in separate reservoirs that each fill and drain by their own rules. Practitioners learn which reserve to spend in a given clash, since a burst of force drawn from the wrong one leaves the body fatally exposed.

rites.name: Torourkoth
rites.text: Torourkoth is a bronze gauntlet of the Martial realm, forged in the seventh age to hold the echoes of disciplines that have been forgotten. When it is struck against a stone plinth, every relic sitting upon the plinths in its vicinity crumbles to dust and its strength is scattered into the bearer as small, random gains in vigor or resolve. Relics that move or strike are instead drawn inside the gauntlet, and a single clench of the fist unleashes each stored technique again, one after another.

rites.name: Karoktazhun
rites.text: Karoktazhun is a crimson-banded war-lens worn by the Thresh-marshals of Kraizhoth, which gathers the wearer's own vitality into a single spectral shaft that cuts clean through the air. Its beam is nursed slowly and strikes in pulses, each pulse scorching whatever it touches according to the bearer's martial strength.

rites.name: Karouzhok
rites.text: Karouzhok is a ring of drifting spectral lanterns that a martial order calls upon in the sixth age of Kraizhoth, each lantern a small pale light that answers its bearer's will. Once bound, the lanterns can be woven into the workings of other tools, turning their stored craft into fresh lights that gather and guard.

rites.name: Garnok
rites.text: Garnok is a grave-bound war-spirit of the Kraizhoth martial realm, a sworn sentinel who returns to the battlefield each time its body falls. Every rebirth hardens its frame a fraction, leaving a permanent edge that its foes learn to dread. Its ember-lattice armor carries the scorched marks of every fall it has endured.

rites.name: Voruktozhok
rites.text: Voruktozhok is a martial discipline of the Kraizhoth Ember-Courts in which practitioners bind their vitality to tallies of minted silver, so each blow taken chips away a token and each coin gathered restores a measure of strength. Its masters teach that wealth is merely stored endurance, and they are judged by how carefully they spend what they have hoarded.

rites.name: Kruggok
rites.text: Kruggok is a martial discipline in the Kraizhoth universe, practiced by wandering duelists of the E6 era who believe any weapon can be unmade into raw fighting spirit. Adepts strike a sealed ritual plinth and the blade dissolves into scattered sparks, which they gather and forge back together into new techniques and tools.

rites.name: Grairkoth
rites.text: Grairkoth is a bell-shaped ward of hardened ash that a Martial-realm duelist calls up from the marrow of their own body, granting a few heartbeats of stone-deep immunity and a rush of speed. Anyone the ward brushes goes rigid as frozen wax and cracks under a slow, cumulative pressure, while stray missiles dissolve to dust against its surface. When its time runs out the ward collapses inward and bursts, its force scaling with how many foes it touched, and every fallen opponent or shattered missile leaves the wielder a little harder to stop.

rites.name: Vhuktouzhak
rites.text: Vhuktouzhak is a mortal war-knot of Kraizhoth's Martial realm, a fighter who carries two bodies that take turns: a sustained living guard and a harsher, hungrier mode that swings harder while spending itself faster. The shift occurs each time the field falls silent, and each form hoards its own satchel of gear, so the warrior must plan which self carries which tool.

rites.name: Krozhaggurn
rites.text: Krozhaggurn is a martial discipline in Kraizhoth's Martial realm, practiced by wandering ash-monks who hold a bound hollow of grief inside the chest. The practitioner sheds a sealed carapace of old oaths and hurls it at foes, where its stored weight of sorrow detonates on impact. Its schools teach that the body is a lever and the carapace is the stone it moves.

rites.name: Krouzharnak
rites.text: Krouzharnak is a crude siege-engine of the Martial realm, a fist-sized mound of refuse that its wielders hurl to scatter ranks. Each sort of Krouzharnak carries a different and unpredictable rot, and when it strikes living flesh it swells into fresh ammunition for the next throw.

rites.name: Druzhokak
rites.text: Druzhokak is a hungry swarm-engine forged in the Martial realm's seventh age, able to strip the matter from any chamber and reshape it into a cloud of brass-winged locusts. Its locusts march forward on command and strike foes with steady, reliable force scaled to the strength of their maker.

rites.name: Torakogun
rites.text: Torakogun is a sealed martial discipline in the Kraizhoth omniverse, practiced in the cold mountain monasteries of the E6 era for seven generations. Its adepts convert bodily vitality into concentrated striking charges that can be unleashed at once, bypassing the slow rhythm of ordinary technique.

rites.name: Vorairnoth
rites.text: Vorairnoth is a sanguine-bound sorcerer-knight of the Martial realm in the E6 era, who forges living crimson sentinels from her own vitality. Each sentinel costs her a fragment of her life-current, and they dissolve back into rot as the hours pass, leaving her mantle heavy with spoiled memory.

rites.name: Drugothar
rites.text: Drugothar is a dread-forged warlord-cult of the Martial realm who fight only with weapons of attack, scorning any protection as cowardice. Their champions carry blades that sing with barely contained force, and their oaths bind them to strike first and endure nothing.

rites.name: Gathukun
rites.text: Gathukun is the root reckoning of the Kraizhoth martial realm, a set of six measures that every fighter, relic, and rite must answer to: force of blow, rhythm of strikes, pace of motion, reach, velocity of projectiles, and the tilt of chance. In the E6 era, masters refine these measures through rare tokens and bargains, so a single warrior's standing can be read as a ledger of adjustments to these six values.

rites.name: Thaikturn
rites.text: Thaikturn is the unseen ledger of the Kraizhoth martial realm, a binding that sorts every spoil of battle into its own pool and grades each one from 0 to 4 in worth. As a warrior advances through the seven ages, the ledger quietly tilts the odds toward finer spoils, so that deeper trials bear sharper gifts.

rites.name: Jorodarde
rites.text: Jorodarde is a concept of the Kraizhoth omniverse, an idea that flickers through the Three Futures where the ending forks and the Library catalogues each outcome on its shelves. It belongs to the Age of the first sovereign, when groves and growing kingdoms first took root and the powers of the Martial Realm were still young.
